subject: POC: What persists from prompts — storage, TTL, and residency (ClearWell)

Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai

Subject: POC: What persists from prompts — storage, TTL, and residency (ClearWell)

Thanks again for the demo today — great conversation. Quick recap and a few specific asks so your security and architecture teams can be comfortable going into the POC.

Recap (short):
- Goal: evaluate Redwood inference for clinical note summarization (structured output, PHI redaction in pipeline)
- POC scope: 3-week sandbox, redwood-hosted cluster in US, sample dataset (anonymized)

Security/data asks we promised to answer: please confirm the desired answers below or correct as needed — we'll route to engineering for any follow-ups.

1) What exactly Redwood stores from a prompt+response?
   - Our default hosted configuration retains: request metadata (timestamp, model id, latency), token-level streaming traces used for debugging, and the raw prompt + model output (for 90 days) unless retention is disabled.

2) Where is that data stored?
   - By default stored in US-east region (multi-AZ). We can pin to a specific region or use a Dedicated/Private deployment for regional isolation.

3) How long is it retained (TTL) and can it be configured per-route?
   - Default TTL: 90 days for prompt+output payloads. Configurable per-customer and per-route (options: ephemeral = 0h, short = 24h, standard = 90d, long = 365d).

4) Controls to avoid storing PII from prompts/responses?
   - Two options: runtime redaction (customer-side SDK filters) and server-side scrubbers (pattern-based redaction + configurable allowlist). We also offer a protocol to drop payloads entirely (no-persist flag) which prevents storage and disables troubleshooting traces for that request.

5) Auditability and access controls
   - Logs and access audited, role-based access via RBAC, and all storage keys can be customer-managed (KMS/HSM) on Dedicated/Private.

Please confirm if ClearWell requires: per-route ephemeral-only storage, customer-managed keys, or an on-premises instance for the POC. If you want, Ben can jump in with a short technical note on how the no-persist flag behaves in the runtime.

Next steps:
- You: confirm which retention profile to test for the POC (ephemeral/24h/90d) and whether your security team needs a Dedicated or Private eval.
- Us: I'll turn this into a one-page privacy options matrix and attach our data-flow diagram (see attachment).

Thanks,

Anna — quick technical note to answer your streaming/no-persist questions. TL;DR: no-persist suppresses persistent payload storage and strips streaming traces from long-term logs; transient runtime buffers still exist for the duration of the request but are never written to persistent storage when the flag is set.

Details (engineer-level):
- No-persist flag: when set on a request, the runtime will:
  1) process tokens in-memory only (KV cache exists in RAM for autoregressive continuity),
  2) avoid writing prompt or response payloads to object storage,
  3) omit the request payload from ingestion pipelines that feed debugging dashboards and long-term archives.
- Streaming traces: we maintain a short-lived stream buffer used to deliver streamed tokens; when no-persist is true that buffer is ephemeral and not forwarded to tracing/analytics collectors.
- Token-level telemetry used for model perf is aggregated (counts, latency histograms) and stored without payload contents. That aggregated telemetry is retained per your chosen TTL for metrics only — it cannot be deconstructed to reconstruct prompt text.
- Audit trails: operator actions (who accessed logs) are stored in audit logs; those logs never include full prompt/response contents unless retention is set to anything other than ephemeral/24h.

Attachment: poC-privacy-options-matrix.xlsx — matrix maps options (ephemeral / 24h / 90d / 365d) to impact on debugging, retention of aggregates, and KMS requirements.

If you want, we can schedule a 20-minute call with our infra lead (Grace) and your security lead to validate the POC config and KMS handshake steps.

-Ben

Anna — thanks, and great questions from security. Short answers to confirm items for the POC we discussed: 

1) POC retention profile: ephemeral (24h) for prompt+response payloads — we will enable server-side redaction and set no-persist=false for requests you want to debug, otherwise no-persist=true for production-like runs.
2) Streaming traces: when no-persist=true streaming buffers are never sent to long-term tracing or written to archives. Short-lived buffers exist only for the duration of the open connection.
3) Permanent audit trails: operator/audit metadata (who accessed request ids, timestamps, model id) will be stored but will not contain prompt/response contents under ephemeral/24h profile.
4) KMS: available on Dedicated/Private. For the POC we can demo an integration using our managed customer key in US-east; if you want customer-managed keys we'll include the handshake steps in the next SOW.

Next steps:
- We will: upload the privacy options matrix and the flow diagram to the shared Drive and provision a sample sandbox in US-east with TTL set to 24h. (Link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/CW-POC/architecture-notes)
- You: please confirm preferred date for the infra call (we can do Mon/Tue next week) and whether your security team prefers a Dedicated eval or cloud-hosted ephemeral run.

I'll follow up with proposed calendar times and a one-pager summary for your compliance team.

Best,
